emulator.title: Try it yourself — a practice copy of Edura
emulator.missHint: Not that one — look for the control with the indigo outline and press it.
emulator.finishedBody: You now know who you act for, how to take attendance, how to confirm students at the classroom door and refuse the one who never passed the counter, how to close a lesson so the teacher's share lands in THEIR wallet with your name on the action, and that you always write under your own name. Your real account works exactly the same way.
emulator.sandboxNote: Everything above is practice — the data and prices are invented, no attendance is recorded and no money moves. The real figures appear on your own screen before any closing.

firstRun.title: First time here? Take 3 minutes
firstRun.body: Before you start, let's walk through a practice copy step by step: take attendance, confirm at the classroom door, close the lesson, and reply to a parent. No real data changes.
firstRun.reopenHint: This tour opens by itself once only. You can reopen it any time from “Guided tour” in the menu.

nav.label: Practice sections
nav.noWalletNote: There is no “Wallet” here — deliberate, not a fault.

screens.actingBody: Everything you do here is recorded in the teacher's record and attributed to you by name: “assistant X on behalf of teacher Y”. That is not a restriction — it is what makes your work visibly yours.
screens.limitsEyebrow: Things that are not yours — and you will not find them
screens.limitWallet: The teacher's wallet and payout requests: you never see them and never request from them.
screens.limitAssistants: Adding or removing assistants: the teacher's right alone.
screens.limitAudit: A capability that is not yours is absent from your screen entirely — not visible and disabled.
screens.counterOnly: At the centre, not in the lesson
screens.settleEyebrow: The step that pays the teacher
screens.settleTitle: Close the lesson and distribute it
screens.settledBody: The revenue was distributed and the teacher's share landed in {teacher}'s wallet — not in your account.
screens.blockedNoAttendance: No attendance is saved yet. The card reads what is saved, so save it first.
screens.blockedNoPresent: Nobody is marked present, so there is nothing to distribute.
screens.settleAction: Close the lesson and distribute EGP {amount} across {n} students
screens.settleHint: The distribution is written to the ledger once, and cannot be undone.
screens.settleArmedHint: Written to the ledger in your name on behalf of the teacher, and credited to their wallet immediately.
screens.doorHint: Confirm counter-checked students at the classroom door. Anyone who has not passed the counter cannot be confirmed here.
screens.counterFirst: Student has not been checked in at the counter — door check-in requires the counter first

welcome.title: Welcome — this is entirely a practice copy
welcome.body: The screens ahead are exactly yours, with invented data: one teacher, one lesson, six students. Press “Got it” and let's go.

actFor.title: You act on behalf of a teacher
actFor.body: Your account was created by them, and every action you take is recorded in their record and attributed to you by name. That is not a restriction — it is what makes your work count as yours.

noWallet.title: And some things you will simply never find
noWallet.body: There is no “Wallet” in your menu, and you cannot add assistants. If a colleague says “I can't find the wallet” — that is correct behaviour, not a fault.

roster.title: Six students
roster.body: Everyone arrives as “Present” by default. Note the two tagged “At the centre, not in the lesson”; we deal with them at the door in a moment.

markAbsent.title: Mark an absence
markAbsent.body: Salma is not here — press the absent control in her row.

goDoor.title: Now the door
goDoor.body: Press “Door check-in” — your main job in “counter + door” mode.

waiting.title: Mariam is waiting at the door
waiting.body: She passed the counter but nobody confirmed her at the hall, so she is still “Waiting”. Without that confirmation she is not counted present and does not enter the distribution.

refused.title: But Karim's case is different
refused.body: Karim never passed the counter — which usually means he has not paid. Try to confirm him and see what the screen says.

toCounter.title: Press “Confirm” in Karim's row
toCounter.body: It will not work — and that is deliberate.

refusedShown.title: The door refused, and it was right to
refusedShown.body: “Student has not been checked in at the counter — door check-in requires the counter first.” Your job here is to send him to the counter, not to find a way round it. That kindness puts an unpaid student inside a lesson that then gets closed.

backToAttendance.title: Back to attendance
backToAttendance.body: Press “Attendance” so we can close the lesson.

settleCard.title: You are allowed to close the lesson
settleCard.body: Yes, it is your right. And closing is what distributes the lesson's revenue — without it the money stays pending.

whoseMoney.title: But the money is not yours
whoseMoney.body: The teacher's share goes to their wallet and the centre's to its books. You have no share in this distribution — if anyone tells you otherwise, they are mistaken.

pressSettle.title: Close the lesson
pressSettle.body: Press the button carrying the amount.

confirmSettle.title: Final confirmation
confirmSettle.body: The distribution is written to the ledger once and cannot be undone.

settled.title: Closed — and in your name
settled.body: The money landed in the teacher's wallet, and the action was recorded as “assistant X on behalf of teacher Y”. If the teacher asks who closed Tuesday's lesson, the answer is there.

identity.title: The message went out under YOUR name
identity.body: Not the teacher's. That is deliberate: most of our students are minors, and no adult may ever speak to one from behind another person's identity. You always speak as yourself.

goNotes.title: And there is a board between you and the teacher

board.title: This is not a chat — these are tasks
board.body: Every note has a status and a line saying who has read it. Anything urgent belongs in “Messages”, not here.

markDone.title: Tick off what you finished
markDone.body: Press “Mark done” on the teacher's note.

done.title: You now know your job and its limits
done.body: You took attendance, worked the door and refused the student who had to be refused, closed a lesson in your name for your teacher's benefit, and replied under your own name. Press “Got it” to finish.

tour.title: A quick tour of Edura
tour.moreHint: On a phone: press “More” first — it's inside there.

welcome.title: Welcome 👋 you're a teacher's assistant
welcome.body: That means you do the teacher's own classroom work — attendance, grades, materials, replying to students — and everything you do is recorded as yours “on behalf of” your teacher. This tour walks you through your day.

messages.title: Messages — this is your main screen
messages.body: Your account opens on Messages rather than a wall of numbers, because this is the job: you are the first line of contact between the teacher and students and their parents.

how.3: Pick the name — the list only shows people you're allowed to message

messages.note: You message as YOURSELF, not as the teacher. And if the student is under 18 their parent can read the conversation, with a clear notice shown to both sides.

attendance.title: How to take attendance
attendance.body: This is most of your work, and it decides who counts when the lesson's revenue is distributed.

how.2: Pick the lesson — every row names the group and the hall
how.3: Anyone "at the centre, not in the lesson" sits in a box above the register — mark them present or absent
how.4: Mark the rest present / absent / excused, then "Save attendance"

attendance.note: If a student shows as “at the centre — did not attend the lesson”, they checked in at the counter but never entered the hall. That is not attendance and does not count in the distribution — even if they paid.

closeLesson.title: And you can close the lesson too
closeLesson.body: Yes — closing a lesson and distributing its revenue is allowed for you, not just the teacher. Without it, the teacher's wallet sees nothing from that lesson.

how.1: After saving attendance, scroll to the "Close the lesson" card under the register
how.2: The button names the amount and the number of students before you press it
how.3: Check the teacher, centre and platform shares

closeLesson.note: This moves money: it is written to the ledger once, cannot be undone, and is recorded as yours on behalf of your teacher. Check the attendance first.

door.title: Door check-in
door.body: If your teacher uses counter + door mode, you are the one doing the second check-in at the hall door.

how.3: Ask for the student's code or scan their card

door.note: Without the door check-in in that mode the student stays “counter only”, is not counted as present, and is left out of the distribution.

classes.title: Your teacher's classes
classes.body: Where you see the groups, their times, their students and their lessons.

how.2: Open the group — it names the centre it belongs to
how.3: See the students, the lessons and the times

classes.note: If you see a notice that a class has no price, tell your teacher — pricing isn't yours to do, and the lesson cannot be closed without it.

grades.title: How to record grades
grades.body: You can add assessments and enter marks exactly as the teacher does.

how.2: Pick the group, then the assessment you are marking
how.3: Type each student’s mark — on a computer, Enter moves you to the next student
how.4: Press "Save grades" in the bar that appears at the bottom

grades.note: The student and their parent see the grade as soon as you save it.

materials.title: How to upload a handout
materials.body: What you upload reaches that group's students only.

how.3: Upload the file and give it a clear name

notes.title: Team notes
notes.body: A to-do board between you and your teacher — not messages: these are things that get done and closed.

how.3: Anyone on the team can mark it done or declined

limits.title: What isn't yours to do
limits.body: Worth knowing now, so you don't go looking for something that isn't there.

how.1: The teacher's wallet and payout requests — not in your menu
how.2: Pricing groups — that's a financial setting, for the teacher or the centre
how.3: Adding other assistants — the teacher only

limits.note: This isn't a lack of trust — it's that money has one door. Everything else in the classroom work is fully open to you.

practice.title: And if you'd rather try it first
practice.body: There's a practice copy you can rehearse on without touching anything real.

how.2: It walks you through your daily work step by step

finish.title: That's it — your turn 🎉
finish.body: The tour is done. Your work starts at “Messages” and “Attendance”. And if you'd rather rehearse first, “Practice” is in the menu.
